en.title: A weekly Search Console analyst bot: three lists of what to fix first
en.summary: The author published two copy-paste prompts: a context interview to brief a bot named “SEO Lead,” and a Search Console Analyst prompt that asks the bot to sign into Google Search Console every Monday at 7am and send three lists of what to fix first. This write-up did not run the prompts, sign into Search Console, or create a bot or routine. The reusable artifacts are the verbatim prompts. The same article claims a six-bot setup, but the article text retrieved in this review only includes the context prompt, Bot 1, and a Bot 2 prompt; Bots 3–6 are not included here.
en.whyItWorks: The author argues that weekly SEO is a repeated set of steps across several tools, and that a scheduled bot can compare Search Console periods and return a short fix list. Claims in the article about $30/month pricing, what xAI’s product can do, the author’s own tests of ChatGPT/Gemini/Perplexity/Grok answers, and which of the three lists “pays” were not independently verified and are not treated as measured results. This write-up did not run either prompt or access Search Console.
workflowSteps: Create a bot (the author says to name it “SEO Lead”) and first send the context-interview prompt preserved verbatim in promptTemplate. It asks the bot to learn the site, offer, customers, location, top pages, money searches, and competitors, and to ask questions one at a time until it can explain the business back. This review did not create a bot or run that interview.

Send the Bot 1 Search Console Analyst prompt, also preserved verbatim in promptTemplate. It asks the bot to sign into Google Search Console every Monday at 7am, compare the last 28 days with the 28 days before, and send three lists (pages that lost the most clicks and the searches involved; searches ranking in positions 5 to 15; pages with many impressions but few clicks), each with a likely reason and a fix, limited to the 10 most important items. This review did not run that prompt or sign into Search Console.

The author says to do the first Search Console pass together, show the bot where you click, and tell it to save the workflow as a routine. That first-run walkthrough was not observed in this review, and no routine was created.

The same retrieved article also contains a separate Bot 2 (AI Visibility Checker) prompt; it is not merged into this case’s promptTemplate, because this case is the Search Console analyst. The article says it covers six bots, but Bots 3–6 were not in the article plain_text retrieved in this review and are not included. Do not run these prompts, connect Search Console, or create routines on Jazfox’s accounts.
en.promptTemplate:
Context interview (author's prompt):

You're going to run SEO for my business. Before you do anything, learn about it. My website is [URL]. We sell [products/services] to [customers] in [location]. Our 10 most important pages are [list]. The searches that make us money are [list]. Our main competitors are [list]. Ask me questions one at a time until you understand the business well enough to explain it back to me.

Bot 1: Search Console Analyst (author's prompt):

Sign into my Google Search Console. Every Monday at 7am, compare the last 28 days with the 28 days before. Send me three lists:
1. Pages that lost the most clicks, and the searches they lost them on.
2. Searches where we rank in positions 5 to 15. These are the closest to page one wins.
3. Pages with lots of impressions but very few clicks. These need a better title.
For each item, tell me why you think it happened and what you'd fix. Keep it to the 10 most important.
en.connectorsAndRoutines: The Bot 1 prompt tells the bot to sign into Google Search Console and to run every Monday at 7am. This review did not check whether that path uses a Search Console connector, a browser sign-in, or something else, and did not enable any connector or routine. No connector name is invented here. The unused Bot 2 prompt in the same article mentions ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Grok, and a Google Sheet; those were not added as connectors for this case.

zh.title: 每周 Search Console 分析 Bot：三张清单告诉你先修什么
zh.summary: 作者公开发布了两条可复制 Prompt：一条是给名为 “SEO Lead” 的 Bot 做业务访谈的开场，另一条是 Search Console 分析 Prompt，要求 Bot 每周一早上 7 点登录 Google Search Console，并给出三张优先修复清单。本稿没有运行这些 Prompt，没有登录 Search Console，也没有创建 Bot 或 Routine。可复用的是原样保存的 Prompt。同一篇文章自称是 6 个 Bot 的完整方案，但本轮检索到的长文只包含访谈 Prompt、Bot 1，以及一条 Bot 2 Prompt；Bot 3–6 未写入本稿。
zh.whyItWorks: 作者认为每周 SEO 是在多个工具间重复的同一套步骤，定时 Bot 可以对比 Search Console 周期并给出一份短的修复清单。文中关于 $30/月定价、xAI 产品能力、作者自己测试 ChatGPT/Gemini/Perplexity/Grok 回答，以及三张清单里哪一张“最值钱”的说法，都未经独立核实，不作为实测结果。本稿没有运行这两条 Prompt，也没有访问 Search Console。
workflowSteps: 先建一个 Bot（作者说命名为 “SEO Lead”），并发送已原样保存在 promptTemplate 里的访谈 Prompt。它要求 Bot 先了解网站、产品、客户、地区、最重要的页面、带来收入的搜索词和竞品，并且一次只问一个问题，直到能把业务复述清楚。本轮没有创建 Bot，也没有运行这场访谈。

再发送同样原样保存在 promptTemplate 里的 Bot 1 Search Console 分析 Prompt。它要求 Bot 每周一早上 7 点登录 Google Search Console，对比最近 28 天与前 28 天，并发送三张清单（点击流失最多的页面及对应搜索词；排名第 5 到 15 位的搜索词；展示多、点击少的页面），每项附可能原因和修复建议，只保留最重要的 10 项。本轮没有运行这条 Prompt，也没有登录 Search Console。
作者说第一次要一起做：打开 Search Console 让 Bot 看你怎么点，并让它把流程保存为 Routine。本轮没有观察这一步，也没有创建任何 Routine。

本轮检索到的同一篇文章里还有一条单独的 Bot 2（AI Visibility Checker）Prompt；它没有合并进本案例的 promptTemplate，因为本案例写的是 Search Console 分析。文章自称涵盖 6 个 Bot，但 Bot 3–6 不在本轮检索到的 article plain_text 里，也未写入。不要在 Jazfox 的账户上运行这些 Prompt、连接 Search Console 或创建 Routine。

source.excerpt:
Grok Bot can now do your weekly SEO while you sleep.

Everyone is using it for their inbox. Almost nobody has pointed it at Search Console.

So I wrote the whole setup. 6 Bots, every prompt, free.
